messages.content:
You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in the body-centred tetragonal space group I-4, number 82, with Hall symbol "I -4". The input cell is not the conventional tetragonal setting: its lattice parameters are a = b = 5.474408 Å and c = 6.66096313 Å, with interaxial angles α = β = 65.7365946° and γ = 90.0°, so the supplied cell is a rhombohedrally distorted, nonstandard setting of the underlying tetragonal lattice. This input cell contains 8 atoms with the declared composition Al₁In₁Cu₂S₄.

The relationship between the input fractional coordinates and the standard I-4 fractional coordinates is given explicitly by q_standard = P q_input + s. The transformation matrix P has first row (approximately 0, −1, −1/2), second row (1, approximately 0, +1/2), and third row (approximately 0, approximately 0, +1/2); the tiny coefficients of order 10⁻¹⁷ to 10⁻¹⁸ in the first and third rows are numerical zeros. The origin shift s is essentially zero, with components of order ±5.6 × 10⁻¹⁷. Thus, to recover the input description from the standard one, one applies the inverse of this near-permutation transformation, which exchanges and combines the crystallographic axes and halves the c-related coordinate.

In the standard I-4 frame, the independent atomic content consists of five orbits. Aluminium occupies Wyckoff position 2c with representative fractional coordinates (0, 1/2, 1/4) and multiplicity 2. Indium occupies 2b at (0, 0, 1/2), also with multiplicity 2. Copper is split between two inequivalent two-fold orbits: one Cu atom of the input formula lies on 2d at (0, 1/2, 3/4), while the other lies on 2a at (0, 0, 0). Sulfur occupies the general position 8g with representative coordinates (x, y, z) = (0.231783, 0.757471, 0.133209), giving eight symmetry-related sulfur atoms per conventional cell. All positional values are quoted to six decimal places, matching the stated rounding precision.

Because the input cell is a nonstandard setting, two small precision corrections are required to describe the real input geometry rather than an idealized exactly symmetric structure. A sulfur atom located in the input frame at fractional coordinates (0.624262, 0.635008, 0.266418) is displaced by (−0.000001, 0, 0), i.e. a one-microcoordinate shift along the first fractional axis. A second sulfur atom at (0.901426, 0.375738, 0.733582) is displaced by (0, +0.000001, 0), a one-microcoordinate shift along the second fractional axis. These corrections are tiny but necessary to reproduce the supplied input positions exactly.

Taken together, the structure consists of an ordered arrangement in which Al, In, and the two crystallographically distinct Cu sites occupy fixed special positions of I-4, while sulfur forms a fully three-dimensional general-position sublattice whose eight equivalent sites are generated by the body-centred tetragonal symmetry. The conventional description contains two Al, two In, four Cu, and eight S atoms, consistent with doubling the declared input composition AlInCu₂S₄ when passing from the 8-atom input cell to the standard I-centred cell.
